clue.text: Burst from a large meal

definitions.meaning: a burst tyre is a sudden puncture, called by the same name
a slap-up feast or binge is informally given the same name

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a sudden tyre burst and, informally, an enormous feast.

clue.text: Fire and water

definitions.meaning: to fire something is to set it alight and scorch it
in Scotland a small stream or brook has this name

explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland and northern England a BURN is a small stream, which is how it means water.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to be on fire; as a Scottish noun it is a brook or stream.

clue.text: Pained expression when top of bed falls off

indicators.note: names the opening letter of the word for bed as the one affected
says that opening letter drops away from the word

parts.note: a couch is a piece of furniture to lie on, a kind of bed

explanation.surface: Someone yelps as the head of a bed collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' and 'falls off' together remove the first letter, C, from COUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sudden pain is exactly this cry.

clue.text: Life after death?

parts.note: not the afterlife but a written account of a person's life, published once they have died

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests religion or the afterlife; the 'Life' is a biography printed in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper notice summarising someone's life story appears after they die.

clue.text: Mild rebuke men receive from instructor

parts.note: tut is a little click of disapproval
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An instructor's soldiers get a gentle telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher or instructor, especially of a single pupil, is this.

clue.text: Chinese takeaway counter?

parts.note: not a shop counter but a Chinese device of beads for counting, including doing subtraction or 'take away'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the counter of a takeaway restaurant; 'takeaway' is subtraction and the 'counter' is a calculating frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The bead-frame calculator, long used in China, counts and subtracts.

clue.text: Pompous colonels can be old gasbags

definitions.meaning: Colonel Blimp was a cartoon of a pompous reactionary old officer, and such men bear his name
the barrage balloons and small airships of earlier days were given this name

explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a 1930s British cartoon figure of a bluff, reactionary officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both reactionary old officers and non-rigid airships, gas-filled bags.

clue.text: An officer's percentage?

parts.note: the warrant that makes someone an officer shares its name with a percentage paid to an agent on sales

explanation.walkthrough: An officer holds a commission in the forces; a salesperson earns one as a cut of sales.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer's rank is conferred by this warrant, and a sales agent's percentage fee is called the same.

clue.text: The shooting of an unknown person?

definitions.text: The shooting of an unknown person?

parts.words: The shooting of an unknown person?
parts.note: not a gunshot but filming an unknown actor to try them out for a part

explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests a crime; in film it means recording, here of a hopeful newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial filming of a would-be actor to judge suitability for a role.

clue.text: Proceeds, after set price has been fixed

indicators.note: something fixed in the sense of rigged or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Takings come in once a price has been agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been fixed' rearranges SET PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Money taken in from sales, the proceeds, is called takings or this.

clue.text: Keep the pot boiling

parts.note: read literally: hold a pan just below a full boil, gently bubbling

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for keeping things going; read literally it describes gentle cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook just below boiling point, keeping a pan quietly bubbling.

clue.text: He drops a line hoping for some response

definitions.text: He drops a line hoping for some response

parts.words: He drops a line hoping for some response
parts.note: not a letter-writer awaiting a reply but a fisherman casting and waiting for a bite

explanation.walkthrough: 'drops a line' suggests sending a note; here the line is a fishing line and the response a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman with rod and line casts and waits for fish to bite.

clue.text: The cost of electricity nowadays?

parts.note: two readings: the price paid for electric flow, and today's going rate

explanation.walkthrough: Electricity flows as a current, so its cost is a pun on today's price.
explanation.definitionFit: The price prevailing at present, and also punningly what electric flow costs.

clue.text: Assume responsibility for, but deceive, an employee

parts.note: to take someone in is to fool them
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A boss takes charge of a worker yet cheats them.
explanation.definitionFit: To take control of or deal with a matter is an idiom for assuming charge of it.

clue.text: Two things a high jumper may carry out from a Chinese takeaway

parts.words: Two things a high jumper may carry out
parts.note: a high jumper may spring upward off the ground

parts.words: Two things a high jumper may carry out
parts.note: a high jumper may also clear the bar using the western roll technique

explanation.surface: An athlete's moves somehow come out of a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The western roll is an old high-jump technique; the 'carry out' also hints at a takeaway order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried pastry filled with vegetables is a staple dish of Chinese takeaways.

clue.text: Petition about a regular payment, so it seems

indicators.note: the word for petition goes round the rest, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: to petition is to apply formally
rent is paid regularly to a landlord

explanation.surface: A request concerning a recurring charge seems to be the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' marks the container; 'Petition' looks like a noun but is read as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning seemingly, as far as one can tell.

clue.text: A number embracing church creed?

definitions.note: the adjective names a famous creed, so creed here stands for the creed's name

indicators.note: the number wraps its arms around the abbreviation for church

parts.note: nine is a number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A count that includes church doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts CE inside NINE. The Nicene Creed, from the Council of Nicaea, is the clue's definition in shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nicene Creed is the statement of Christian belief drawn up at Nicaea.

clue.text: Hard to place

definitions.meaning: concrete or jelly that has become firm has done this
to put something down in position

explanation.definitionFit: The word means having become firm, and as a verb to put something in position.

clue.text: Timetable for education in a German school

indicators.note: the education abbreviation goes inside the German word

parts.note: Schule is German for school

explanation.surface: A timetable for learning in a school in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue expects a little German: the word for school there is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan of times for events is a timetable.

clue.text: The man from whom Samuel imbibed wisdom

definitions.text: The man from whom Samuel imbibed wisdom

parts.words: The man from whom Samuel imbibed wisdom
parts.note: in the Bible, the boy Samuel was raised and taught by the priest at Shiloh

explanation.walkthrough: In the First Book of Samuel the priest at Shiloh brought up the young prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical priest of Shiloh raised and instructed the boy Samuel.

clue.text: When soccer wars erupt, they're frightening

indicators.note: things that erupt burst out in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Football fan violence is a scary sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupt' rearranges SOCCER WARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw figures in fields exist to frighten birds away.

clue.text: Horses right to take for a ride outside

indicators.note: the word for swindle goes outside the abbreviation

parts.note: to sting someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: Horses on the right are taken out on a hack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts STING round R. A trainer's horses are collectively a string.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse owner's or trainer's stable of horses is called a string.

clue.text: Strange thing, gin and bitters, for producing sweet songs

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the birds, standing in for the plural noun

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: bitter is a kind of British beer, so bitters are ales

explanation.surface: An odd drink of gin and bitters gets people singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges THING GIN; then add ALES, as bitter is a type of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: These small birds are famed for singing beautifully, often at night.

clue.text: Sailor a short distance nearer the stern

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
FT, foot, abbreviated, is a short length

explanation.surface: A seaman stands a little closer to the back of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term meaning towards or behind the stern of a ship.

clue.text: Heartless head cook

indicators.note: without its heart, so the middle letter of the word for head goes

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle letter, I, from CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional cook in a kitchen bears this title.

clue.text: Long Island in Scotland? No!

parts.note: in Scotland a small island has this name, yet as a length it is anything but long

explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes Long Island, New York; in Scots an island is an inch, and an inch is a tiny length.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish name for a small island, and a very short unit of length.

clue.text: A Spaniard is killed while hunting

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the youth of myth, standing in for his name

parts.note: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man from Spain dies on a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite was killed by a boar while hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The handsome youth of Greek myth was gored to death by a wild boar on a hunt.

clue.text: The monkey's brother

definitions.meaning: a South American monkey; the 's stands for is
a friar of the Franciscan order with a pointed hood

explanation.walkthrough: The monkey is named after the friars, whose hoods its markings resemble.
explanation.definitionFit: Names both a hooded friar of a Franciscan order and the South American monkey named after them.

clue.text: Tug used in river flood

indicators.note: the word for tug is placed inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to lug is to haul or tug

explanation.surface: A tugboat works on a flooded river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' marks the container; the Dee is a river in both Scotland and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A great overwhelming flood, as in the biblical one.

clue.text: Day of sport — night of comedy

definitions.meaning: the Glorious ..., 12 August, opens the British grouse-shooting season
Shakespeare's comedy is titled after the night ending Christmas festivities

explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, when British grouse shooting begins; Twelfth Night is Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal names the grouse-shooting opening day and the Shakespeare comedy's night.
